## Contract review brief — PR #35740 @ `2d25ef2edc25ad7b6a5b129c3a479f2d7b123406` (card #35570)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35570: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #35740: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `2d25ef2edc25ad7b6a5b129c3a479f2d7b123406`
  · the check-runs on `2d25ef2edc25ad7b6a5b129c3a479f2d7b123406`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/coordinator.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/objectstack.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/c35570/l2/pr-35740/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感。这是给协调者看的规则：以后你说「再开一个 area:X」，就由已在座的座位加一个分区，不会再另开座位。这个方向和你的原话一致。
- 出错会怎样：新加的两句话互相打架。一句说"一个项目在一条车道最多一个座位"，另一句又说"你明说开座位就开新座位"。协调者如果只照前一句读，就可能拒绝你明说的"再开一个座位"。改几个字就能修好。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。卡线程改好这一句后我再看一次增量。

## 席位核对 — REWORK (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `2d25ef2edc25ad7b6a5b129c3a479f2d7b123406` · 2026-11-20T05:07Z

- **Shape** — draft, base `main`, 1 commit, 4 files, +8/−4. Merge-base `a457b515`, which already carries the byte ratchet (#35712). `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35740`: **GOVERNED, Tier S**, 12 lines. `Fixes #35570`, `Clause-②: no`, `Rule-change: ruled`. The Ruling-ref is the 2026-11-19 15:40Z 「你应该用同一个座位，之需要不同的分区啊」, which ruling record 7030459053 transcribes, with the 04:21Z dispatch order. The 15:40Z sentence is also in this project's standing record from that hour, so the quote is corroborated.
- **The byte raises are exact.** I measured `git show <ref>:<path> | wc -c` at the merge-base and at the head:

  | File | Base | Head | Delta |
  |:--|--:|--:|--:|
  | `area-lease.md` | 6401 | 6586 | +185 |
  | `coordinator.md` | 3781 | 4267 | +486 |
  | `lanes/objectstack.md` | 2270 | 2505 | +235 |

  Each `CEILINGS` row moves by exactly its delta, with headroom 0, and its row comment names 7030459053. No other row moves, which is the ruled-raise form the ratchet header allows.
- **What matches the card.** The `area-lease.md` line separates the in-seat file-cluster 区 from the `area:*` product label, and says that one label may be split into several areas or folded into one. That is the card's item 2. In `coordinator.md`, a new `area:*` for a seated lane goes to that seat: it goes on the intake line, it is partitioned under `area-lease.md`, and ⛔ no new seat thread, post, mailbox or patrol is opened. In `objectstack.md`, intake is a property of the seat. The 「L2 新席坐空座」 qualifier keeps the backlog-seat rule as it was, and stops the line from reading as "new intake ⇒ new seat". That is the misreading the card names.
- **S1 (should-fix, blocks this ACCEPT): the added text contradicts itself on a maintainer's explicit seat order.**
  - `coordinator.md` §一 line 8 and `lanes/objectstack.md` 形态 line 8 state an absolute: 「一个项目在一条车道至多一席」 / 「一个项目在本车道至多一席」.
  - The very next `coordinator.md` line opens a new seat 「只在维护者说的是座位(「开座位」「再开一个座位」)或该车道没有本项目的席时」. Its first arm is a second seat in a lane this project already seats, which the absolute forbids.
  - The unchanged text keeps that path too: `lanes/objectstack.md:36` 「开席、加席、收席由维护者召唤」, and `project-forms.md:15` 「一车道多席:协调者取 🟢 行写本账号的那一席」.

  A coordinator reading line 8 strictly would refuse a maintainer's 「再开一个座位」, which is the reverse of the 15:40Z error and just as wrong. The card's own wording has the same tension. The fix is to make the absolute a default with its one exception, in both files. For example:
  - `coordinator.md`: 「一个项目在一条车道默认一席,维护者明说开座位才加席。」
  - `objectstack.md`: 「一个项目在本车道默认一席(维护者明说开座位才加席);…」

  Then re-measure, and move the two rows by the new delta under the same ruling record. A few bytes either way, and the record covers these files.
- **Gates** — at this head: 26 success, 23 skipped, 0 failure. The ratchet is green at headroom 0.
- **Next** — after the fix, I read the delta here. Landing stays Tier S: a same-head `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (brief 7030854050), then the seat's adoption. The L2 should judge S1 too.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2d25ef2edc25ad7b6a5b129c3a479f2d7b123406`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/coordinator.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/objectstack.md + scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card 35570 (body and all five comments), the PR body and file list, the net diff of the head against `main` (4 files, 8 insertions, 4 deletions), and the head's check-runs. The skill files the changed lines cite were read in the tree at the head. Nothing was built, tested or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- Published accept set and public surface: nothing moves. All four paths are `.claude/**` or `scripts/pm/**`, and neither ships in a package. Right.
- What a coordinator opens on a maintainer order: an order that names another `area:*` for a lane the project already seats no longer opens a seat thread, seat post, mailbox or patrol. It becomes an intake write on the seated seat and a partition under `area-lease.md`. Right: this is item 1 of the card's "What changes" and the 15:40Z sentence.
- When a new seat opens: on the maintainer's word seat, or on a lane with no seat of the project; the L2 backlog add-open is kept by name. Right: without that carve-out `coordinator.md:9` would contradict `coordinator.md:13`, which stands on `main` with its own no-ask clause.
- `coordinator.md:15`, qualified to `L2 新席…`: narrowed, and nothing is lost. On `main` its subject already was the add-opened review seat (rows by claim, sign-off when the queue drains). Sitting an empty post and opening a mailbox stay stated for every other seat in `coordinator.md:7`, `seat-lifecycle.md` (坐席同笔) and `area-lease.md` (开席, step 1). Right.
- Vocabulary: 区 is fixed as a file-cluster lease inside a seat and `area:*` as the card's product-area label. This agrees with `lanes/objectstack.md:23-24` (a 区 belongs to one seat; its name lives in the lease table and the claim's Area line) and with the label table in `SKILL.md` (one `area:*` per public card). Right.
- Two new terms, 接卡行 and 接卡面, enter three files. No file on `main` defines them. See N1.
- Instruction-surface byte budget: three `CEILINGS` rows rise, 6401 → 6586, 3781 → 4267 and 2270 → 2505, which is +185, +486 and +235, +906 in all. Read with `git show REV:PATH | wc -c` at the merge-base a457b5157 and at the head: each file measures exactly its new ceiling, and each base size equals the old row. No other row moves and `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` stays empty, so this is the ordinary ruled raise and not a cross-file move. Right, on the ruling check in ④.
- `main` since the merge-base: the three files on `main` today carry the same blob ids as the diff's base side, and the newest `main` commit on the ratchet script is the merge-base itself. The net diff against today's `main` is the same 8 insertions and 4 deletions.

### ② Semver level

No changeset, label `skip-changeset`. Right: the diff publishes nothing from any released package, which is the one case AGENTS.md keeps that label for. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head. The PR body declares Clause-② as `no` and the metadata protocol as `none`. Both are right: no published accept set widens or narrows, no public surface grows, and nothing a metadata author can write changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: 49, every one concluded, each success or skipped; none red and none pending. `Test Core (1/10)` was still running at the first read and concluded success by the last one, as did its aggregate `Test Core`.
- Dev deviation, commit trailer: answered. The head commit ends with the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes. That is the repo rule, not a departure from it.
- Dev deviation, local exit code of `check:pm-dispatch-gates` not captured: answered by the head's check-runs. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates` both concluded success.
- Dev note, `check:doc-formula-expressions` answered exit 3 before the lint closure was built: answered by `Lint · docs & code guards`, success.
- "No test owed": agreed. The diff is text plus three integer rows, and the gate that reads those rows ran in CI on this head.
- Open question, whether the one-seat rule also binds `l2-review` seats: answered A, the L2 backlog rule stands as written. The ruling speaks of an area label on a seated lane. The add-open is standing text on `main`, the card orders no change to it, and the new line keeps it by name. Binding review seats would be a new ruling on a new card; nothing in this PR waits on it.
- Out-of-scope finding, 接卡行 is not defined in `seat-post-protocol.md`, reported with no carrier: taken up as N1 below. It needs a carrier, so the adopting seat files the follow-up card.
- The ruling of record, comment 7030459053, was written by the thread that holds the claim. It says so, and it says its first three quotes are relayed from the card body and were not re-read in the chat. Those quotes match the card body character for character, and the dispatch order matches regrade comment 7030325025; both of those were written by another session, the seat's. The dispatch order was read first-hand, and the PR body links its thread. Not escalated. It is noted so that whoever reads the quoted sentence before landing knows which half is first-hand.
- PR author is the fleet App, so no off-relay author note is owed.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- Security: the dev's "none" is agreed. No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour; the hunks say which seat takes a card and where the seat records it. No `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The scenario the change is accepted against: the maintainer says 「再开一个 area:fleet」 to a project that already holds a `repo:objectstack` seat. On the tree at this head the coordinator reads `coordinator.md` 一 before it opens a seat thread (the section's own read cue), and line 8 hands the order to the seated seat and forbids the four things the incident produced. The seat's lane file calls it an intake change and an in-seat partition, never 加席. The first rule line of `area-lease.md` tells the lease 区 from the label. The card's "Done when" holds.

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/coordinator.md`
- Line 8 holds against `main`. `project-forms.md:15` already has the coordinator take the one seat whose 🟢 line names its account on a multi-seat lane. `cross-repo-coordination.md` lets a lane split into several seats (a sustained backlog splits by repo, through a PR), and it never makes one project the holder of two. `area-lease.md` (开席, step 2) has the coordinator open a 区 thread, and the ⛔ list rightly leaves that out.
- Line 9 is a necessary condition ("只在…才"), so `coordinator.md:11-12` (a lane held by another account; never sit another seat) keep binding. I tried the account switch at the usage wall, a same-seat successor session, a seat move, the epic and director seats and a newly declared lane. Each is either not a new seat or a lane with no seat of the project, so line 9 blocks none of them.
- Line 15: see ①.

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/objectstack.md`
- Line 8 agrees with the file's header (current state lives in the seat post, never in this file), with 范围 (the lane's range stays the whole repo; a seat's intake is the areas the maintainer named, which `SKILL.md` already makes the pick order) and with 「可多席、多账号」 on line 7. The pointer to `coordinator.md` 一 resolves.

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md`
- Line 7 agrees with the lines under it: boundaries follow files and packages, never titles or vocabulary (line 10), and the lease table maps 区 to paths to a thread (line 12). "可切成几区,也可并入现有区" is what file-cluster boundaries imply for a label.

`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (implementing), against the raise discipline in its own header, sentence by sentence:
- "authorized by the ruling of record that orders text into the file": comment 7030459053 is a fleet-transcribed maintainer ruling with who, words and where, the carrier `untrusted-text.md` names. The 04:21Z order dispatches this card, and the card's "What changes" names these three files and this rule. Stands.
- "quotes that ruling comment's id and the measured byte delta in its body": the PR body does, per file. Stands.
- "moves the row in the same PR by at most that delta": each row moves by exactly its file's measured delta. Stands.
- "content no ruling ordered is paid for by deletion": every added sentence is item 1 or item 2 of the card, or reconciles one of them with standing text (the L2 carve-out, the `L2` qualifier, the pointer). Nothing else was added. Stands.
- The three row comments are one line each, and their old and new values and the ruling record id are true.

Nits. None changes correctness or the card's contract. Each is left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card, because a fix in these files moves the head.

- N1 (nit, follow-up card): 接卡行 is where `coordinator.md:8`, `lanes/objectstack.md:8` and `area-lease.md:7` put a seat's intake, and `seat-post-protocol.md` does not know the line. Its stub list names four items plus the patrol and mailbox keys, its refresh occasions (坐席、串行队/cron 改、撞墙、移交) do not include an intake change, and a takeover restates the body from the four-section template, where an unnamed line can be dropped. The follow-up names the line in the stub and adds the occasion. It cannot ride this PR: that file is outside the card's fence, and its ceiling has no ruled raise.
- N2 (nit, accepted deviation): `coordinator.md:8` states a cap (至多一席), and `coordinator.md:9` then names 「再开一个座位」 as an order that opens a seat. On a seated lane that is a second seat of the same project, and it is the only case in which the first arm adds anything to the second. `lanes/objectstack.md:8` repeats the cap without the exception, while line 36 keeps 加席 by the maintainer's summons. Both sentences are the card's own, in the card's order; the card's scenario does not reach the case, and a reader meets the exception on the next line. The seats rewrite that rebases onto this text can say "one by default".
- N3 (nit, accepted deviation): the partition outcome is spelled three ways: 自开一区或并入现有区 in `coordinator.md:8`, 可切成几区,也可并入现有区 in `area-lease.md:7`, 在席内分区 in `lanes/objectstack.md:8`. None names the case `area-lease.md:9` keeps: below the threshold there is no partition and cards are claimed one by one. `coordinator.md:8` defers to `area-lease.md` by name, so that file governs, and the seat's re-judgement on its line 8 still applies.
- N4 (nit, next edit of the script): the comment above `CEILINGS` (`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:68-80`) still says that every ceiling is its file's size at the re-basing base, that four rows are marked and that no number is a raise. After this diff seven rows are marked and three are ruled raises. The comment's last sentence is what licenses the three row comments, and no gate reads the paragraph.
